newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Money for Bangladesh worker dumped in S'pore ditch.
newsitem.headline: Money for Bangladesh worker dumped in S'pore ditch.

text.p: Money and good will have poured in for illegal Bangladeshi worker Mohammed Bashar, who was dumped in a Singapore drainage ditch after being injured in a building site accident, a Bangladesh diplomat said on Monday.
"I was with him on Sunday and by then he had received about S$1,300 (US$915) and many visitors," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

Bashar, 24, was dumped in the ditch after being struck on the head by a descending lift. He lay writhing in agony for two hours before his cries for help attracted the attention of a passing army jeep.

Bashar was paralysed permantly from the waist down in the December accident. His plight came to light on Friday after police confirmed they had arrested one man and were hunting for a second in connection with the incident.
Staff at the hospital where Bashar is being treated told Singapore's Sunday Times newspaper they had received more than 50 calls to ask about his condition and make donations.

It quoted several visitors as saying that they were appalled such a thing could happen in Singapore, which has been cracking down recently on companies, many of them in the construction industry, who employ illegal workers..
Bashar's medical bills have been met so far by Singapore authorities, said the Bangladesh official.
He told Reuters that the second man had been arrested, but police spokesmen were not immediately available to confirm this.
"We are in touch with the Singapore authorities about how they will deal with this inhuman behaviour. We want stern action taken to ensure such things never happen again," the diplomat said.
Bangladesh was talking to Singapore about compensation payments for the injuries, he added.
Singapore deports illegal workers, but police said on Friday that no decision had been made on whether to send Bashar home.
Bashar said he found after arriving in Singapore that the work permit he paid S$6,000 for back home was a forgery.
